title: The Bond Deepens
text: “Never mind Wolf—did you two even listen? Hurry up and run and go call for help!”

And apparently their attack wasn’t just brute force, either—they’d aimed for weak points and concentrated their strikes to deal fatal blows to the monster, I say. The battle itself lasted about ten minutes, or so I heard. The slaves ended up battered and bruised from fighting so valiantly. As for that out-of-place monster Father and the others had encountered earlier, it turned out to be the very same stray monster we’d heard about at the tavern. In any case, the slaves joined forces, defeated the monster, and—gasping for breath—raised a unified cry of victory, knocking their fists together in triumph. After the battle, Father scolded them for disobeying orders, and while all three looked appropriately remorseful, it seems the whole ordeal only deepened their bond. According to Father, he looked exhausted mainly because he was already dreading the next time they’d ignore his orders. According to Rabbit Guy, they’d twisted logic at him, insisting that abandoning one’s master to flee simply wasn’t something a slave could do. Apparently the mutt lizardman agreed as well. I could understand that kind of loyalty myself, honestly. If Big Sister had been fighting alongside Father and encountered some powerful monster, wouldn’t she probably have done the exact same thing?
“Honestly… I think it’s brave, but it’s also kind of maddening.”
“I can understand the feeling, indeed. It just shows how much they adore Father.”
Even I doubt I’d find it easy to choose flight in a similar situation.

“That doesn’t make it okay, though… well, I’ll give Wolf, Sion, and Theo a proper talking-to later. Everyone’s leveled up decently, so we should probably spend some time practicing combat for a while.”
Level isn’t everything, indeed.
“Right, I heard earlier why you’re fighting. If you’re going to face the Waves, I won’t hold back my help.”
“Yes, for Iwatani-sama’s sake, I’ll do my best, betting everything on this sword.”
“Wauu!”

And so, all three slaves seemed brimming with motivation regarding the coming battle with the Waves, indeed. It seemed the mutt lizardman and Rabbit Guy had settled in well enough that they’d started looking into whether they could join other acts over at the circus. They’d even come asking Elephant and me for sparring practice. Their bond truly seemed to have grown stronger, indeed.

And so, in a flurry of activity, about two weeks passed. It seemed we were finally nearing the time when we could reliably meet up with Older Sister. And so, bringing Big Sister and her friends along, we arrived at the abandoned village of Lute Village.
With the wind whistling by, we ended up waiting for Older Sister to notice us.
“So this is Raphtalia-chan’s village.”
“Yes.”
“I see… Everyone worked so hard trying to rebuild it together, but…”
“You got hit by slave hunters, right?”
“That’s right…”
“Bubu!”
Keel was energetically protesting something to Father.
“Yeah, I know. I want to gather everyone as quickly as possible too.”

Over the past two weeks, while stopping through various towns, Father had managed to find a few people from Big Sister’s hometown. Sadly, it wasn’t everyone, though. What’s more, many of them had suffered abuse, so the cost of treatment was nothing to scoff at. That said, lately we’d secured a treatment area inside one of the tents, and Father and I had started healing people with recovery magic and the like. Under the condition that it not be used for peddling, he’d also been picking up how to make medicine. Apparently it would come in handy for treating Wolf and Rabbit Guy too, so Father had been studying late into the night.
“So their sister’s coming here, huh.”

By the way, Sion was tagging along this time, indeed. Apparently, when Father was about to head out with Big Sister and the others, Sion had stopped him and asked where they were going, then insisted on coming along too.
“So I hear. Something on your mind, Sion?”
“No… mind if I just look around this area a bit?”
“Sure. As long as you actually come back.”
“Order it through the slave crest. Tell it not to go past the next town over.”
“I’m not really fond of setting restrictions like that, but fine.”

Father seemed to be giving orders through the mutt lizardman’s slave crest. After that, the mutt lizardman claimed to be “taking a walk” and shot off in a straight line toward parts unknown. Eventually… as the sun began to set, indeed. While we had a fire going, Older Sister came shuffling up from the sea in her orca form.
“Sadeena-oneesan!”
Big Sister noticed Older Sister and dashed over to her.
“Oh my! If it isn’t little Raphtalia-chan!”
Older Sister pulled Big Sister into a tight embrace as she ran up.
“Thank goodness. I’ve been looking all over for you, you know… Are you hurt anywhere? Looks like everyone else is here too.”
“Yeah.”
“Bubuu!”
Big Sister’s friends rushed over to Older Sister and began recounting everything that had happened. Then Older Sister approached Father, her benefactor.
“Huh? Wait, so Raphtalia-chan’s ‘Big Sister’ is—”
“Oh?”
Father let out a surprised sound upon seeing Older Sister.
“Well, if it isn’t you again! Who would’ve guessed you were the one looking after Raphtalia-chan and the others! Sister here had no idea!”
Older Sister spoke as though she already knew Father somehow. Whatever could that be about?
“Father, do you know her, I wonder?”
“Yeah. On the way back from buying slaves, I sometimes stop by taverns with the envoy from Siltvelt, and I’ve run into her here and there in various towns.”
“Aww, Sister just thought you seemed like some sort of bigwig, but who’d have guessed you were actually a Hero! Sister sure didn’t catch on.”
“You kept trying so hard to get me to drink with you, too. And you had no problem getting the people from our side completely wasted.”

Come to think of it, there’d been that time the Siltvelt envoy came home dead drunk, propped up by Father. There’d also been another instance where some subordinate of a monster merchant went down in similar fashion. So it seemed they’d all crossed paths with Older Sister before. Was that it, then? Perhaps whenever we visited one of those taverns in Melromarc that admitted demi-humans and beastfolk, there was a chance Older Sister happened to be there too.
“Aww, but you were fine even after drinking the booze Sister recommended, so of course Sister remembered you—what a lovely encounter, don’t you think?”
Older Sister was being remarkably friendly. Goodness, it seemed that even while touring around with the circus, Father managed to run into her fairly often.
“It was rough on my end, though, having to carry drunk people home afterward.”
Father gave a wry smile.
“So, would I be right in calling you Sadeena-san?”
“That’s right! Thank you so much for taking care of Raphtalia-chan and the others. Sister really appreciates it.”
“Yeah.”
“Raphtalia-chan… Sister will take care of you in place of your parents, okay?”

This flow of events… it bore quite a resemblance to a much earlier loop—the one right before defeating the main body of the Crimson Swine, when the very next loop after heading to Faubrey had gone this way.

“The rest of the village is here too, but there’s no lord, no one with any real authority… I wonder what we should do. Maybe it’d be best to take everyone to another country. I don’t think we should rely on the Hero too much, either.”
“Um… wait, Sadeena-oneesan. Um, listen. Shield Hero-sama has been helping search for everyone in the village. That’s why I want to rebuild the village… I swore it on that flag, that day.”

Big Sister said this with a smile plastered stiffly on her face. This part of the flow was the same as before, it seemed. Older Sister was probably considering protecting Big Sister and the villagers, but judged rebuilding to be too difficult.
“But you see…”
“You needn’t worry about that. We’ve already secured a shelter for everyone over in Zeltoble. As for rebuilding, it can wait until after the mess in Melromarc gets sorted out.”

It was simply a matter of holding out until the Queen returned, indeed. As for the Three Heroes Church… well, this time Father wasn’t playing Saint of the Sacred Bird, but that could be dealt with one way or another. Apparently being too saintly wasn’t good either, so it seemed best to aim for roughly the standard set back in the very first world. Come to think of it, things had gone smoothly the last time we’d looped through this too. So perhaps that level of effort would suffice. Well, worst case, Father and I could always march into Faubrey, prove the Three Heroes Church to be a heretical cult, and drag the Queen back by force—then rebuilding the village would be entirely possible, indeed.
